messages:
Alex: Quick async check — need a short compatibility sanity pass on the generation endpoint. Observed weirdness around stop sequences + max_tokens + temperature/top_p interplay, and logprobs getting null in the final token. Anyone able to help triage?

Maria: On it. Can you paste a minimal repro and the expected vs actual?

Alex: Repro (curl to dedicated canary):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"stable-7b","input":"Tell me a short poem:\n","max_tokens":20,"stop":["\n\n"],"temperature":0.0,"top_p":0.0,"logprobs":5}'
```
Expected: deterministic (temp=0/top_p=0 => greedy), stop triggers when sequence matches, returned tokens length <= max_tokens, and `logprobs` present for each returned token.
Actual: intermittent runs return >max_tokens (2–3 tokens over) or fewer tokens with the final token having `logprobs: null`. Happens on canary in us-west; not heavy load.

Chen: Can you paste a trimmed response example?

Alex: Example response (sanitized):
```json
{
  "id":"g-xyz",
  "tokens":["The"," end"," of"," the"," song"],
  "logprobs":[{...},{...},{...},null],
  "stop_reason":"stop_sequence",
  "usage":{"prompt_tokens":8,"completion_tokens":5}
}
```
Note the last logprobs entry is null and tokens length sometimes is 5 even though max_tokens=20 (so overflow not huge, but >expected in other runs).

Simone: I haven't seen null logprobs on final token before. Two suspects: 1) streaming truncation / final chunk boundary; 2) request normalization: `top_p:0.0` is odd — our API historically clamps top_p to [1e-6,1.0] in some codepaths which may change sampling kernel selection. Also stop vs max_tokens precedence might be implemented inconsistently between batch and streaming backends.

Raj: FYI older v1 clients didn't set top_p (implicit 1.0). If they set temp=0 but leave top_p unset we might be combining greedy intent with a non-greedy top_p. Backcompat layer sometimes rewrites fields; maybe a bug there. We should define canonical semantics: when temp==0 && top_p<=eps treat as greedy.

InfraBot: Canary status: runtime v2.4.1 deployed to us-west (20% canary). No CPU/GPU abnormalities; no infra errors logged in last 15m.

Maria: Proposal: a) normalize incoming params in the parser: treat `top_p < 1e-5` as exactly 0; b) enforce stop sequence matching before enforcing max_tokens so we don't silently exceed tokens; c) guarantee `logprobs` array length equals tokens length; use explicit `null_reason` only for truncation mid-byte/encoding and surface that in the response.

Alex: Agree with that. Adding: when we clamp top_p->0 we should also route to deterministic kernel path (no sampling). That will make behavior reproducible for greedy clients. Documentation update required for legacy behaviour.

Simone: I'll open a PR that adds normalization in request parser + unit tests (non-streaming and streaming). Tests include: deterministic replay with seed, `temperature=0/top_p=0`, and stop sequences at token boundaries and multi-token stops.

Chen: I'll review the PR and add streaming regression tests — specifically ensure streaming chunks don't drop the final `logprobs` object. Also check the streaming code path that applies stop checks: streaming should perform stop detection as soon as the stop sequence is emitted and mark `stop_reason` accordingly without nulling logprobs.

Raj: I'll run evals on quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) to see if quantization + KV cache affects tokenization near stop boundaries — could explain intermittent overflow. Will also check if compilation/kernel selection differs when top_p is clamped.

Maria: I'll draft a short API note for Console/docs: clarify greedy semantics, explain how `top_p`/`temperature` normalization works for v1 vs v2 clients, and document when `logprobs` can be null. Also will add a short migration snippet for teams still using unconstrained `top_p`.

Simone: Code review ping @Chen @Raj when PR is up — will include test harness and a simple curl-based integration test against canary.

InfraBot: Incident monitor: none.

Alex: Action items summarized: Simone -> PR for normalization + tests; Chen -> streaming unit/regression tests + review; Raj -> quantized eval + kernel check; Maria -> docs + migration note. Aim for merge by EOD Friday. Post PR link and any blockers here. :thumbsup:

Chen: Sounds good — will try to review within the day. If streaming fix is non-trivial I might request a small canary-only hotfix first.

Raj: If I find a kernel mismatch I'll attach perf diffs; might be a ripple to runtime teams.

Alex: Thanks all — pinging in case anyone sees this later. We'll keep this thread as the coordination point.
